source.title: Does DINOv3 Set a New Medical Vision Standard? Benchmarking 2D and 3D Classification, Segmentation, and Registration
source.authors: Che Liu; Yin-Da Chen; Hao-Yuan Shi; Jinpeng Lu; Bai-Liang Jian; Jia-Zhen Pan; Linghan Cai; Jia-Yi Wang; Jie-Ming Yu; Ziqi Gao; Xiao-Ran Zhang; Long Bai; Yun-Di Zhang; Jun Li; Cosmin I. Bercea; C. Ouyang; Chen Chen; Zhi-Wei Xiong; Benedikt Wiestler; Christian Wachinger; James S. Duncan; Daniel Rueckert; Wenjia Bai; R. Arcucci

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or wrong-document issue.
record.tranche_reason: Extends investigation of scaling to medical vision tasks using DINOv3 size and resolution comparisons, but measures downstream task performance rather than language-model held-out loss.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates medical-task performance across DINOv3 sizes and resolutions and explicitly reports inconsistent scaling. It does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy, fit loss power laws, test extrapolation, or optimize parameter/token allocation. Rows focus on the reported size- or resolution-scaling results; unrelated benchmark comparisons and task scores without a reported scaling implication are omitted.
record.test_reason: The study compares frozen DINOv3-S/B/L encoders on many medical downstream tasks. That bears on V6, whether downstream performance improves predictably with model scale, in a vision-transfer setting. It measures no pretraining loss, fits no power law, and varies neither data nor compute, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested. Input-resolution scaling is a test-time input choice, not parameters, tokens or compute, so it maps to no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that DINOv3 is a strong off-the-shelf medical baseline, especially for CT and X-ray. It degrades on WSI, EM and PET, and its scaling with model size and resolution is task-dependent and not reliably beneficial.
record.recipe_differences: Uses DINOv3 vision encoders at several sizes and resolutions for medical downstream tasks; does not fit language-model held-out-loss scaling laws or test compute-optimal training allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Task, dataset, modality, and input resolution affect the reported scaling behavior; NIH-14 performance peaks at 512×512 and then declines.

fits_no_version.finding: NIH-14 AUC for all sizes peaks at 512×512 input resolution and declines at higher resolutions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream performance of frozen vision encoders is non-monotonic in input resolution.

record.problems: The scaling evidence is based on downstream medical-task metrics, not held-out pretraining loss; no power-law fits, exponents, extrapolations, or compute-optimal allocations are reported. The evaluation focuses on the DINOv3 family and frozen encoders. Some scaling claims are qualitative, and the resolution result is given without numeric values in the text. Registration tables report standard deviations, but uncertainty for the scaling comparisons is otherwise not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were omitted due to the 60-row cap. Other benchmark scores and baseline comparisons that do not report a model-size or resolution scaling result were left out.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss or power-law fits.
Shape at fixed parameter count not varied.
No loss and no power-law form fitted in any modality; only three released model sizes are compared downstream.
Predictability from pretraining loss; any fitted trend; data or compute scaling; models beyond three sizes (the 7B teacher is not evaluated).
No fitting choices, exponents or schedules examined.

missing.what: WSI per-size AUC: Camelyon16 S 0.840 / B 0.805; Camelyon17 S 0.854 / B 0.792
RSNA-Pneumonia AUC by size: S 0.8667, B 0.8666, L 0.8708 (flat)
EndoVis18 by size: binary IoU 86.05/89.04/92.19 and instrument IoU 39.86/46.37/63.97 (monotonic); EDD2020 average Dice 71.50/73.56/72.90 (non-monotonic)
EM per-size VOI/ARAND values showing large gains with size
Resolution × size curves for NIH-14 and RSNA, values not in the text

record.verdict_notes: V5 is dropped: no loss or power-law form is measured. The DINOv3 S/B/L models are released checkpoints, likely distilled from the 7B model, so size is confounded with training recipe. Only three sizes are tested, all with frozen-feature probes. The reader's 'absent' states for EM and PET conflated poor performance against other methods with lack of a scaling effect; the within-family numbers show size gains.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model pretraining loss or power-law loss fits are measured.
No small-run loss fits or predictions of substantially larger runs are tested.
No fixed-compute parameter/token allocation or compute-optimal split is tested.
The study varies model size and resolution, not depth, width, or architecture at a fixed parameter count.

Tests medical-vision downstream performance across model sizes and resolutions, not held-out pretraining loss or whether the same fitted power-law form and exponents hold. Does not test repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer across training regimes.
Measures downstream task performance across model sizes and resolutions, but does not test whether it is predictable from pretraining loss or fit a predictive relationship.
Reports task-dependent and non-monotonic downstream performance scaling, but does not test fitting choices, exponents, parameter-count conventions, training schedules, or compute-optimal splits.

relationships.condition: EM neuron segmentation, MSD average Dice, NIH-14 AUC at 256px
relationships.reason: Larger frozen DINOv3 encoders score monotonically better: EM error falls sharply S→L (R13), MSD average 69.0→71.3 (R12), NIH-14 AUC 0.7788→0.7865 (R2).
relationships.display_finding: Scaling encoders reduced EM segmentation error sharply from S to L, increased MSD average Dice from 69.0 to 71.3 and raised NIH-14 AUC from 0.7788 to 0.7865.

relationships.reason: Gains over S exist but are non-monotonic; B beats L or dips below S (R5–R11, R14).
relationships.display_finding: Larger variants sometimes improved over S, but B could outperform L or fall below S depending on the task.

relationships.condition: WSI classification (S vs B) and cardiac registration
relationships.reason: Camelyon AUC drops from S to B (R3). CAMUS and ACDC registration Dice show no size effect beyond SD (R16, R17, R19, R20).
relationships.display_finding: Camelyon AUC fell from S to B, while CAMUS and ACDC registration Dice differences stayed within standard deviations.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Medical-vision scaling comparisons across the tested tasks and resolutions
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that scaling does not transfer consistently: resolution performance can decline, and model-size trends differ across tasks (R1, R3, R11, R12). These are downstream task results, not direct tests of held-out-loss power laws.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: AUC declines beyond the reported NIH-14 resolution peak, and the report says larger models can underperform smaller ones on WSI classification (R1, R3).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Larger models are generally beneficial on CT-RATE and typically outperform smaller ones on MSD, but the report says the CT improvement is not always monotonic and MSD results are mixed (R11, R12).
